findings.title: Refresh token accepted from JSON body, and both tokens returned in JSON response — HttpOnly cookie protection undermined
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the `req.body.refreshToken` fallback and stop spreading `...tokens` into JSON responses (register/login/otp/verify/refresh all do this). Rely solely on the HttpOnly cookies; the client already uses cookie-based refresh via authFetch. Keeping tokens out of JS-readable responses makes XSS token exfiltration materially harder.

findings.title: No refresh-token rotation state or revocation: logout/compromise cannot invalidate a live refresh token (7d TTL)
findings.suggested_fix: Rotation reissues a fresh pair (good) but old refresh tokens stay valid until 7d expiry — /logout only clears cookies server-side and there is no token-version/jti denylist. Add a `tokenVersion` (or jti) column on users, embed it in the refresh JWT, check+increment on logout/password change/admin password reset (server/routes/admin.ts:289 sets a new password but any stolen refresh token still works).

findings.title: 12 admin mutation endpoints have no Zod validate() middleware (hand-rolled, inconsistent checks)
findings.evidence:
router.put('/users/:id/password', async (req, res) => { const { newPassword } = req.body; if (!newPassword || typeof newPassword !== 'string' || newPassword.length < 6) {...}
// also unvalidated: /users/:id/role (317), /users/:id/points (344), /products (372), /products/:id (404), /orders/:id/status (511), /coupons (593), /coupons/:code (635), /orders/:id/tracking (803), /reviews/:id/approved (841), /contact-messages/:id/status (717), /settings (935)
findings.suggested_fix: Add Zod schemas in server/validators (adminPasswordSchema, roleSchema, pointsSchema, productUpsertSchema, orderStatusSchema, couponUpsertSchema, trackingSchema, approvedSchema, messageStatusSchema, settingsSchema) and pass to validate() like cart/orders/auth routes already do. Admin-only status lowers exploitability but parseInt()-coercion gaps (e.g. `parseInt(stockQuantity) || 0` silently zeroes stock on garbage input) are real logic bugs.

findings.title: POST /api/contact and POST /api/contact/newsletter validated manually, not with shared Zod schemas
findings.suggested_fix: Use validate(contactSchema)/validate(newsletterSchema) for consistency; also add an email format check to /api/contact (currently any non-empty string passes as email) and a dedicated contact rate limiter — only the general 600/15min limiter applies, so message-table flooding at ~40/min is possible.

findings.title: CSP scriptSrc includes 'unsafe-inline' and imgSrc allows plain http:
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'unsafe-inline' with nonce- or hash-based script policy (Vite bundles are external files; inline usage is small). Drop `http:` from imgSrc to avoid mixed-content loading of attacker-influenced product image URLs. Weakens XSS containment if an injection ever lands.

findings.title: PUT /api/admin/users/:id/role returns the full DB row including the bcrypt password hash
findings.suggested_fix: Destructure out `password` before responding (`const { password, ...safe } = updated`), matching the pattern used in GET /users (line 275-278). Admin-only, but the hash then sits in browser devtools/proxies/logs unnecessarily.

findings.title: Unauthenticated GET /api/payment/verify lets the caller pick the verification provider via query param
findings.evidence:
const explicitProvider = req.query.provider as any;
const verifyResult = await paymentRouter.verifyPayment({ authority, status, amountTomans: order.total, orderId: order.id }, explicitProvider);
findings.suggested_fix: Verify against the provider recorded on the order (the one that issued the authority) instead of trusting `req.query.provider`; a caller could steer verification to a gateway where the authority/amount check differs. Low severity because amount+authority are still checked, but it removes a free parameter.

findings.title: JWT secrets only require 10 chars and are only blocklisted against 6 known placeholder strings
findings.suggested_fix: Require min 32 chars and reject low-entropy secrets (e.g. entropy/length heuristic) rather than a fixed blocklist. Also assert JWT_ACCESS_SECRET !== JWT_REFRESH_SECRET (currently not checked — reusing one value for both silently passes validation). .env on disk contains all expected keys (PORT, DATABASE_URL, JWT_ACCESS_SECRET, JWT_REFRESH_SECRET, ZARINPAL_MERCHANT_ID, ZARINPAL_SANDBOX, GEMINI_API_KEY, APP_URL, SMS_API_KEY, SMS_PROVIDER, SMS_TEMPLATE_ID, BALE_BOT_TOKEN, BALE_ADMIN_CHAT_IDS) — values not inspected.

findings.title: Auth cookies lack __Host- prefix and explicit Domain scoping relies on default
findings.suggested_fix: Rename to `__Host-accessToken`/`__Host-refreshToken` (requires Secure, Path=/, no Domain — all already true in prod) to pin cookies against subdomain-injection. Flags themselves are correct (HttpOnly, Secure in prod, SameSite=Strict in prod / Lax in dev).

findings.title: All limiters skipped only in test, but general limiter keying trusts a single proxy hop — consider keying login limiter by IP+phone
findings.evidence:
const limiter = rateLimit({ windowMs: 15*60*1000, max: 600, skip: () => process.env.NODE_ENV === "test" || env.NODE_ENV === "test", ... });
app.set("trust proxy", 1);
findings.suggested_fix: Distributed low-and-slow credential stuffing stays under 5 req/min/IP. Add a secondary per-account counter on /api/auth/login (keyGenerator including req.body.phone) so a botnet rotating IPs still gets throttled per victim phone number.
